ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: Given: Point $P$ is a point on segment $AC$, $BP=DP$, $AB=3$, $CD=7$. As shown in Figure 2, if $\angle A = \angle C = \angle BPD \neq 90^\circ$, find the length of $AC$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:}\\
Since $\angle A=\angle C=\angle BPD$, $\angle A+\angle B=\angle BPD+\angle CPD$\\
Thus, $\angle B=\angle CPD$\\
Since $BP=DP$\\
Therefore, $\triangle APB \cong \triangle CDP$\\
Thus, $AB=PC=3$, $AP=CD=7$\\
Therefore, $AC=\boxed{10}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In Figure 2, the diagram shows A, P, and C lying on one straight horizontal segment, with P between A and C. Segment AB rises from A to B on the left, segment BP connects B to P, segment PD connects P to D on the right, and segment CD connects C to D. Thus the left triangle is triangle ABP and the right triangle is triangle CDP. The angle markings in Figure 2 indicate the relevant equal angles at A, at C, and at P between BP and DP. Reasoning: Since A, P, C are collinear, the angles above line AC satisfy ∠APB + ∠BPD + ∠CPD = 180°. In triangle ABP, ∠A + ∠B + ∠APB = 180°, so ∠A + ∠B = ∠BPD + ∠CPD. Given ∠A = ∠BPD, subtracting gives ∠B = ∠CPD. Also given ∠A = ∠C and BP = DP. Therefore triangles ABP and CDP have two corresponding equal angles and a corresponding non-included side equal, so triangle ABP ≅ triangle CDP by AAS. The correspondence is A ↔ C, B ↔ P, and P ↔ D. Hence AB corresponds to CP, so CP = AB = 3, and AP corresponds to CD, so AP = CD = 7. Therefore AC = AP + PC = 7 + 3 = 10.
